claim: Every new attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. For a consumer project targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, none of the generated formatters or resolvers carry `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. Yet `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and is valid on classes there. So the acceptance criterion 'All generated code is decorated' is unmet for those targets with no compatibility reason. netstandard2.0 is a common target for MessagePack DTO libraries. The derived criterion allows conditional emission only when the attribute does not exist on a target. The same guard is repeated in EnumTemplate.tt, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt, ResolverTemplate.tt and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt, and in their .cs counterparts.
